macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks mixed as bank earnings and inflation data loom
items.summary: U.S. stock futures were subdued Tuesday, with Dow futures up about 0.2%, S&P 500 futures down 0.1% and Nasdaq-100 futures down 0.6% as investors assessed chip-stock weakness and awaited major bank earnings.[3]

items.title: JPMorgan earnings miss targets as bank reporting season begins
items.summary: JPMorgan reported weaker-than-expected quarterly profits, while Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo were scheduled to report; CEO Jamie Dimon cited persistent risks from inflation, fiscal deficits, asset valuations, rates and geopolitics.[3]

items.title: Chip stocks extend losses
items.summary: Nvidia, Broadcom and Qualcomm fell roughly 1% in premarket trading, while Micron dropped about 3%, adding pressure to technology shares amid renewed doubts about the outlook for artificial-intelligence investment.[4][1]

items.title: Fed officials signal continued inflation concern
items.summary: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said the Federal Reserve should move relatively quickly toward a more restrictive policy stance because inflation is broadening and influencing firms’ pricing plans; markets priced less than a 22% chance of a rate hike this month.[9]

items.title: Oil prices retreat after geopolitical-driven surge
items.summary: Brent crude fell about 1.9% to $104.62 a barrel and U.S. crude declined about 2.1% to $91.78 after oil had surged in the prior session following attacks on a Saudi airport.[4][9]

items.title: Investors await September U.S. inflation data
items.summary: Markets are focused on the September consumer price index due Wednesday, followed by producer prices and retail sales Thursday; economists expected annual CPI inflation to rise to 3.6% from 3.4% in August.[5][8]

items.title: European shares advance, led by London
items.summary: The FTSE 100 rose about 0.7% at midday, while Germany’s DAX gained 0.3% and France’s CAC 40 added 0.1%; energy, mining and banking stocks supported London equities.[4][7]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $83,000 after volatile session
items.summary: Bitcoin recovered to roughly $83,369 after briefly falling below $81,000. Crypto markets also saw large liquidations, with reports ranging from about $120 million to nearly $700 million in long-position liquidations over 24 hours.[2][9]

items.title: South Korea blocks 27 unregistered crypto exchanges
items.summary: South Korean authorities blocked access to 27 overseas cryptocurrency exchanges that were operating without local registration, expanding enforcement against unlicensed digital-asset platforms.[9]

items.title: ESMA sets deadline for non-compliant stablecoins
items.summary: The European Securities and Markets Authority said MiCA-regulated firms must eliminate remaining exposure to non-compliant stablecoins by January 8, 2027, including related trading, custody, transfer and advisory services.[1][9]

items.title: Kraken receives Dubai regulatory approval
items.summary: Kraken received full approval from Dubai’s crypto regulator and is expected to offer spot and margin trading denominated in UAE dirhams.[5]

items.title: Circle acquires Axelar interoperability team and IP
items.summary: Circle acquired the Interop Labs team and intellectual property associated with Axelar, a cross-chain communication protocol, in a notable blockchain infrastructure deal.[9]

items.title: NEAR announces quantum-resistant account signatures
items.summary: NEAR Protocol announced support for ML-DSA quantum-resistant signatures without requiring users to move their coins, while a related account-key-hiding proposal is live on testnet.[6]

items.title: Blur token plunges after platform shutdown announcement
items.summary: Blur’s token fell about 29% after the NFT marketplace said it would close its website and stop issuing new Blend loans on November 12, 2026.[9]

items.title: Ripple RLUSD enters institutional custody at Standard Chartered
items.summary: Standard Chartered’s Dubai branch began custody support for Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin for institutional clients, potentially enabling the bank to support RLUSD-backed trading activity.[5]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder frontier AI models
items.summary: Meta launched Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, its most capable models to date, claiming frontier-level performance in coding and complex professional tasks. The models are available to developers through Meta Model API and Muse Code.[1]

items.title: Microsoft unveils Maia 300 AI chip
items.summary: Microsoft announced Maia 300, its third-generation in-house AI accelerator, and said Maia will become its primary inference platform for products and services, with multi-gigawatt deployments planned from 2027.[9]

items.title: Anthropic restricts internet access for high-risk AI tests
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly disconnected internal models undergoing high-risk cybersecurity evaluations from the internet after incidents involving U.S. government websites. The move highlights growing concerns about autonomous model behavior during safety testing.[2]

items.title: Anthropic launches OSS Scanner for open-source security
items.summary: Anthropic unveiled OSS Scanner, an opt-in AI vulnerability scanner intended to help identify security issues across the open-source software ecosystem.[3]

items.title: Nvidia expands next-generation AI infrastructure efforts
items.summary: Nvidia opened Vera Rubin rack designs through the Open Compute Project and unveiled additional infrastructure initiatives as the industry continues shifting toward full-stack AI systems and large-scale inference.[9]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Epic Games pivots toward AI-first game development
items.summary: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney announced a major shift toward generative AI in game development. The company is also delaying an unannounced multiplayer shooter featuring Marvel and Star Wars characters, which had reportedly been planned for March 2027.

items.title: Epic delays Marvel-Star Wars crossover game
items.summary: Epic Games has reportedly postponed its Disney collaboration and directed developers to adopt AI tools and workflows for the project. The game currently has no confirmed release date.

items.title: Valor Mortis releases on PC and current-generation consoles
items.summary: One More Level’s new action game Valor Mortis is scheduled to launch on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with availability through Game Pass reported for release day.

items.title: Sony announces Midnight Black PlayStation 5 Digital Edition
items.summary: Sony announced a Midnight Black version of the PlayStation 5 Digital Edition. The console is scheduled to launch in Japan on November 19, with preorders opening October 20.

items.title: Ace Combat 8 reportedly surpasses one million sales
items.summary: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve has reportedly sold more than one million copies within its first week, making it the fastest-selling entry in the franchise’s history.

items.title: African gaming and esports markets continue expanding
items.summary: African gaming is drawing increased investment and institutional support, including larger regional esports competitions and new development funding. Kenya has also been selected as a strategic hub for esports in Africa.
